page: Microsoft Azure E96as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor built on x86_64 architecture. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with two threads per core, operating at 3.525 GHz. Cache sizing includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is 672.0 GB, which yields 7.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no local storage, requiring network-attached solutions such as Azure Premium Storage for disk operations. It contains no GPU hardware acceleration and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate substantial multi-threaded processing power. In stress-ng testing, the multi-core score reached 129540.53, placing the instance in the top 10% tier, alongside a single-core score of 2915.08. Geekbench testing yielded a single-core score of 1732.0 and a multi-core score of 18509.0, with sub-test scores of 51206.0 in Clang software compilation and 87781.0 in ray tracing. Memory throughput capability is demonstrated in Redis benchmarks, achieving 84.05 million SET operations per second.

Cost efficiency is centered around compute consolidation and large memory allocation per node. Without onboard NVMe storage, disk throughput is bound entirely to network storage limits, presenting a tradeoff between storage performance flexibility and remote disk latency. The hardware configuration makes the instance suitable for large relational database management systems, in-memory caching clusters such as Redis, enterprise data analytics, and memory-intensive batch processing.
